notation.meaning: Demand and supply in the market example
Partial derivatives of demand and supply

blocks.md: Sometimes two variables are tied together by an equation you cannot easily solve for one of them — an equilibrium condition, an indifference curve. The implicit function theorem says you can still find how one responds to the other: the slope is minus the ratio of how sensitive the equation is to each. It is the formal tool behind comparative statics: how does the equilibrium price move when demand shifts?

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: It turns any equilibrium condition or first-order condition into predictions about how outcomes respond to changes.
